audit_findings.title: Post-ATC debt cost is absent from the FY2025 owner-earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed scale is $338.745 million cash consideration, $330.0 million initially borrowed, and $234.0 million of revolving debt outstanding at June 30, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 OE anchor excludes both ATC earnings and the interest on acquisition financing, while the bridge and share count use the post-acquisition date.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company drew down $350 million from the revolving credit facility to partially fund the acquisition and for working capital needs.
audit_findings.explanation: The pre-acquisition earnings/post-acquisition balance-sheet mismatch is demonstrated. Missing interest overstates value, but missing ATC cash earnings understates it. Because ATC net income and parent-attributable owner earnings are not separately filed, the net valuation effect and its materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Build a June 2026 or trailing-twelve-month parent-attributable OE reconciliation that includes ATC operating cash economics, acquisition-related working capital and capital expenditure, and incremental interest; then rerun all scenarios on the matching June 2026 balance sheet.

audit_findings.title: Parent earnings may be mixed with consolidated joint-venture cash-flow adjustments
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; relevant filed scale is $67.725 million of FY2025 NCI net income and $819.562 million of consolidated-JV revenue versus the $136.7 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Any NCI share of consolidated depreciation, capital expenditure, working-capital movements or other cash-flow adjustments left in OE increases the numerator without adding corresponding Parsons common shares.
audit_findings.evidence: For the joint ventures we control, we consolidate all the revenues and expenses in our consolidated statements of income (including revenues and expenses attributable to noncontrolling interests).
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated calculation error: the record establishes that the cash-flow statement is consolidated, but does not show whether the valuation removed NCI portions line by line. The filed NCI and JV activity are large relative to the anchor, so the possibility may affect value, but the actual adjustment is unavailable.
audit_findings.action: Produce a parent-only OE schedule for every cash-flow adjustment, supported by consolidated-JV statements and ownership percentages, and rerun after removing all cash economics attributable to NCI.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may add cash unavailable to Parsons common shareholders
audit_findings.magnitude: $79.806 million of the $266.044 million cash balance was consolidated-JV cash; complete removal would reduce value by a computed $0.68 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds consolidated cash dollar for dollar even though JV assets are restricted to the relevant ventures and part of their economics belongs to NCI.
audit_findings.evidence: The assets of the consolidated joint ventures are restricted for use only by the particular joint venture and are not available for the Company’s general operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The inclusion of restricted JV cash as freely available excess cash is demonstrated, although the correct Parsons economic share is unresolved. Even the conservative upper-bound adjustment of removing all $79.806 million would lower the $18.71 base value to about $18.03 and the $20.62 bull value to about $19.94, still far below the $47.58 market price.
audit_findings.action: Identify the legally distributable Parsons economic share of each consolidated JV's cash, subtract associated operating requirements and NCI claims, and use only the resulting excess amount in the next bridge rerun.

audit_findings.title: Joint-venture guarantees are contingent claims ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $168.2 million filed exposure at June 30, 2026; full-face arithmetic equals $1.44 per share, while realistic loss is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A guarantee call would reduce parent cash or future OE and therefore the common-equity bridge, unless already reserved or recovered from partners or insurers.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we had $184.4 million of letters of credit and guarantees that relate to joint ventures.
audit_findings.explanation: No present loss is demonstrated, and the filing reports that JV funding is infrequent and not anticipated to be material. The exposure is nevertheless forward-looking and should be monitored. A hypothetical loss of the entire filed face amount would reduce the bull value from $20.62 to about $19.18, which would not change the current valuation conclusion, but face value is not a realistic-loss estimate.
audit_findings.action: Update the exposure each quarter and obtain instrument-level data on overlapping letters of credit, partner recourse, indemnities, reserves, collateral and probability-weighted loss before recognizing any bridge adjustment.

audit_findings.title: The convertible-note share ceiling does not match the cash-settled claim modeled in earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: 8.500480 million excess gross shares, 7.3% of the modeled denominator; removing them produces a computed 7.8% increase in per-share values
audit_findings.mechanism: The denominator assumes gross share settlement even though the $800 million principal is cash-settled, while OE appropriately retains note interest; only conversion value above principal can create contingent dilution, subject to the capped call.
audit_findings.evidence: Upon conversion, the Company will settle the principal amount of the 2029 Convertible Notes converted in cash and will settle the remainder of the consideration owed upon conversion in cash, shares of the Company’s common stock, or a combination thereof, at the Company’s option, with such amount of cash and, if applicable, shares of common stock due upon conversion based on a daily conversion value calculated on a proportionate basis for each trading day in a 50-trading day observation period.
audit_findings.explanation: The denominator inconsistency is demonstrated and conservatively understates value. Removing all 8.500480 million gross conversion shares would reduce the denominator from 116.897119 million to 108.396639 million and raise bear, base and bull values to approximately $17.46, $20.18 and $22.24. Even the corrected bull value remains $25.34 below the $47.58 market price, so the valuation conclusion does not change.
audit_findings.action: Rerun with 108.396639 million shares before contingent conversion dilution; model shares only for conversion value above the $94.11 conversion price, incorporate the capped-call offset through its $131.7575 cap, and retain after-tax note interest unless a scenario actually assumes conversion.
